hypothesis: The squaring-macro episode (delete sq, obstruction is the formula tax, repair is re-adjoining sq) changes access observables (min formula size 7 vs 3 for x^4, fibre mass 5 vs 14 at the bound) while every registered screen partition on the shared tree universe is identical across grammars and the delete/re-adjoin round trip is the identity. Min size is therefore not a function of the (q, K) data at this bound: a delete-repair fact outside (q, K), living on the generator/process coordinate the close-out already quarantined as process-relative.

controls.description: Grammars, size bound, targets, screens, and the verdict rule are written in core.py before enumeration.
Base-grammar trees must be a subset of extended-grammar trees, so screen comparisons are on literally the same objects.
Min sizes must equal the banked US-2/US-3 values (2^(n+1)-1 = 7 vs n+1 = 3 at n=2); this instrument reuses the episode, it does not invent one.
Delete then re-adjoin must restore the access table exactly; otherwise the episode is not the banked loop.
outside_fact_found, all_reduce, and inconclusive are all valid passing runs.

gates.criterion: Grammars, screens, targets, and verdict rule specified before the run.
Both grammars enumerate to the bound and the extension is strictly larger.
Base trees embed in extended trees.
x^2 and x^4 are reachable in both grammars at the bound.
All three registered screens (q_den, q_size, q_depth) have recorded invariance rows.
Delete then re-adjoin is the identity on the access table.
Verdict is outside_fact_found, all_reduce, or inconclusive.
No kill of the representability reading, no continuum claim, no LLM, no new master object.
